newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle market remains still - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle market remains still - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets near midday remained still, with no reported trades amid light buyer inquiry, feedlot sources there said.
Packer bids were light and ranged from $69.00 to $70.00 per cwt against asking levels of $72.00 to $73.00.
Fed cattle prices last week dropped $2.00 to $71.00, compared with the previous week.
Sales this week were not expected until Wednesday, with packers said to have sufficient live supplies. The industry also will be watching to see what happens with beef demand, market sources said.
Talk circulated that beef prices could soften this week.
However, unusually warm weather over the weekend could have resulted in strong demand as consumers fired up backyard barbecues for one last time before colder weather moves in, sources said.
"Everyone's waiting to see what happens with beef prices," a Kansas cattle feeder said.
Beef prices at ahead of midday Monday were quoted down $0.01 to $0.21 per cwt on 42 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
